publications.name: Building Domain-Specific LLMs Faithful To The Islamic Worldview
publications.summary: Proposed a comprehensive framework for building domain-specific LLM systems aligned with Islamic values. Evaluated prompt engineering (zero-shot, few-shot, instruction-based), RAG over 54k Hadith dataset, and fine-tuning GPT-3.5 on IslamQA. Fine-tuning on Hadiths (10k) + IslamQA (400) achieved best F1 of 0.402 with 0.078 embedding distance.
publications.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) have demonstrated remarkable performance across numerous natural language understanding use cases. However, this impressive performance comes with inherent limitations, such as the tendency to perpetuate stereotypical biases or fabricate non-existent facts. In the context of Islam and its representation, accurate and factual representation of its beliefs and teachings rooted in the Quran and Sunnah is key. This work focuses on the challenge of building domain-specific LLMs faithful to the Islamic worldview and proposes ways to build and evaluate such systems. Firstly, we define this open-ended goal as a technical problem and propose various solutions. Subsequently, we critically examine known challenges inherent to each approach and highlight evaluation methodologies that can be used to assess such systems.

context.research_premise: Existing LLMs exhibit Western bias and hallucinate on domain-specific religious content. Investigated whether prompt engineering, RAG, and fine-tuning could align models with the Islamic worldview.
context.methodology_detail: Evaluated GPT-3.5, GPT-4, Llama-7B, and Llama-70B across zero-shot, few-shot, and instruction-based prompting. Built RAG system over 54k Hadith dataset using OpenAI ada-002 embeddings. Fine-tuned GPT-3.5 turbo on Hadiths (10k) and IslamQA (400 questions).
context.eval_strategy: Used BERTScore (precision, recall, F1) and embedding distance (cosine similarity via ada-002) on 100 randomly selected IslamQA questions, comparing model responses to scholar-generated answers.
context.key_results: Few-shot prompting consistently best across all models. Fine-tuning GPT-3.5 on Hadiths + IslamQA achieved F1=0.402, best overall. RAG alone did not show significant improvement over prompting. Paper also implemented guardrails using RAIL (Reliable AI Markup Language).
context.my_contribution: Developed the evaluation frameworks to measure alignment and accuracy (BERTScore + embedding distance metrics). Presented the research at the NeurIPS 2023 MiML Workshop.
context.author_position: 3rd of 3 authors. Research conducted during B.Tech (2023), published December 2023.

projects.name: HVAC Copilot
projects.description: On-device voice + vision agent for field HVAC technicians. Gemma 4 E4B runs 100% on-device via Cactus Python on MacBook Pro M4; three thin clients (Chrome, iPhone Safari, Rokid AR glasses via WebRTC) share one assistant runtime over six function-calling tools.
highlights: Built assistant runtime + 6-tool function-calling surface on Gemma 4 E4B running 100% on-device via Cactus Python; one runtime drives three clients (Chrome, iPhone Safari over LAN, Rokid AR glasses over WebRTC).
Authored a streaming token sanitizer handling Gemma 4's three tool-call opener variants so raw tool markers never leak into user-visible transcripts.

Designed explicit on-device vs online boundary — 5 local tools + 1 gated cloud escalation (search_online_hvac) with amber UI banner, enforced in both the system prompt and the dispatcher. Top 10 Finalist out of 200+ builders.

context.problem_space: US HVAC technician shortage (~110K unfilled roles per BLS); senior-to-junior first-time-fix delta is 20+ points. Junior techs in the field need a senior on every truck. Cloud-first solutions fail: job sites have unreliable connectivity and customer data shouldn't leave the device.
context.architecture_decision: One assistant runtime shared across three thin clients. On-device by default; a single explicit online-escalation tool is the only networked path out. Boundary enforced twice — once in the system prompt, once in the dispatcher (query_kb cannot auto-chain into search_online_hvac).
context.key_innovation: Streaming token sanitizer for Gemma 4's three tool-call opener variants (<|tool_call|>, <|tool_call>, <|tool_call_start|>). A stateful _StreamSanitizer class buffers partial markers and only emits clean suffixes to the client while the tool-loop still captures structured calls.
context.my_contribution: Built the assistant runtime (Gemma 4 tool-call parsing for all 3 opener variants, 3-pass tool-loop, _StreamSanitizer), tool dispatcher + 6-tool contract, voice pipeline (Silero VAD + faster-whisper STT + Kokoro TTS for the Rokid path), 8-hop latency instrumentation, and FastAPI + WebSocket server. Tash Matsusaki built the Rokid AR integration; Amogh D. Prasanna did pre-hackathon HVAC technician research.
context.measured_performance: Model load 4-6s. TTFT bare-model 217ms; with full HVAC system (~935 prefill tokens) 3.9-4.5s on CPU-prefill. Decode ~17 tok/s. Rokid end-to-end ~20s. Cactus has not yet shipped an ANE-compiled model.mlpackage for Gemma 4 E4B — TTFT expected to drop under 1s on M4 with zero code change once they do.
context.outcome: Top 10 Finalist out of 200+ builders at Y Combinator × Cactus × Google DeepMind Voice Agents Hackathon (Apr 19-20 2026, SF). No category prize. 4-person team with Amogh D. Prasanna, Tash Matsusaki, Evode Manirahari.

projects.name: Auto-Eval3D
projects.description: ViewFusion spatial coherence evaluator for generative 3D Gaussian Splat worlds. Text prompt → Marble-generated 3D world → inside-out 4-view capture → Gemini 2.5 Pro multi-view reasoning → coherence score.
highlights: Built an automated text-to-evaluation pipeline: user prompt triggers World Labs Marble API to generate a Gaussian Splat world, SparkJS + THREE.js render it, an inside-out 4-view WebGL camera rig captures interior viewpoints, and Gemini 2.5 Pro evaluates geometric consistency.

Implemented the inside-out camera rig handling COLMAP's Y-down coordinate space (Math.PI X-axis rotation, camera placed at world origin with eye-level offset, 20-frame settle per view for SparkJS Gaussian re-sort).

Encoded ViewFusion-style structured reasoning as a 3-phase XML prompt (spatial pre-alignment → category analysis → scored findings with defined failure tiers). WINNER — Best Scientific & Engineering Application.

context.problem_space: Generative 3D (Marble, text-to-3D diffusion) produces impressive-looking worlds that are often spatially incoherent — bookshelf viewed from the back becomes a stone wall, objects change scale between views, floors float. No automated benchmark for multi-view coherence existed. 2D metrics (FID, CLIP score) don't capture multi-view inconsistency.
context.architecture_decision: FastAPI proxy + vanilla JS frontend + Gemini via Vertex AI + SQLite persistence. No framework on the frontend — the work is almost entirely imperative WebGL + THREE.js code, so React/Vue would be overhead. SQLite because evaluation history is small and local-first.
context.key_innovation: Inside-out camera rig: places camera at world origin (where Marble worlds are generated from), rotates in place to look in 4 directions, captures each view with a 20-frame settle and dual-render to let SparkJS Gaussian re-sort. The naive approach (orbit camera around bounding box) photographs a blob in a void and produces useless evals — a bug I caught and fixed post-hackathon.
context.post_win_bug_fix: After winning, re-audited the evaluation traces. The demo's Medieval Library scored 1/10 'severe Janus artifact' — but the score was actually critiquing bad screenshots (camera outside the scene), not a bad 3D world. Mar 30 commit 7ee621e rewrote the capture rig to live at world origin and rotate in place. Honest engineering discipline: kept auditing after the prize was awarded.
context.viewfusion_prompt_structure: Three explicit XML phases. (1) <spatial_thinking>: force pairwise cross-image analysis (1-2, 1-3, 1-4, 2-3, 2-4, 3-4) with 6 artifact categories listed. (2) <thinking>: category-by-category evaluation. (3) <answer>: 1-10 score with threshold tiers (1-3 severe, 4-5 noticeable, 6-7 minor, 8-9 high, 10 perfect). Temperature 0.2. Backend parses each XML tag via regex and stores all three fields in SQLite.
context.my_contribution: Solo author. FastAPI backend (387 lines) with 4 endpoints, vanilla JS frontend (674 lines) with the inside-out camera rig, SQLite CRUD layer, ViewFusion prompt. All 3 commits: Mar 28 submission, Mar 28 README + UML, Mar 30 camera-centering + prompt-injection + async-blocking fixes.
context.outcome: WINNER — Best Scientific & Engineering Application track at BigThink × World Labs Hackathon (Mar 28 2026). Prize: $150 World Labs credits.
context.event: BigThink × World Labs Hackathon, Mar 28 2026. In-person judging in an auditorium. Seven category tracks awarded.

projects.name: Wine Voice AI
projects.description: Self-directed product build: an npm-workspaces monorepo pairing a grounded voice wine advisor with an immersive 3D retail boutique. WASD-navigated first-person shop, VRM-model sommelier NPC, and a consultation state machine driving Vertex AI streaming + Google Cloud TTS.
highlights: Built a retail-grade voice wine advisor monorepo: three npm workspaces — wine-boutique-world (3D boutique with NPC sommelier), wine-voice-explorer (sandbox chat), and packages/wine-ai-core (shared library: catalog loading, NL parsing, Vertex AI SSE streaming, Cloud TTS, proxy server).

Kept Gemini grounded in the catalog with zero hallucinated bottles via local regex-based parsing of shopping signals (color, region, varietal, price, occasion) + filtered catalog injection + system-prompt invention ban. Added follow-up carry-forward and progressive relaxation.

Designed a resilient voice pipeline: Chrome Web Speech Recognition with 14 wine-specific transcript auto-corrections ('pinot newar' → 'pinot noir'), 1.6s silence timeout for hands-free turn-taking, premium Cloud TTS voice (en-US-Neural2-D), and a graceful fallback ladder (Cloud TTS → browser speechSynthesis → silent text).

context.problem_space: Wine retail is a product-discovery problem disguised as a catalog problem. Shoppers want to describe a scenario ('housewarming for my sister, light reds, under $40') and get grounded recommendations — not filter-UI checkboxes. Static catalogs require SKU literacy shoppers don't have; chat interfaces hallucinate bottles that don't exist.
context.architecture_decision: Monorepo with npm workspaces so retrieval + voice + LLM logic lives in one package (packages/wine-ai-core) and both apps import from it. Vite middleware wraps the proxy server for dev; standalone Node server (app.mjs) exposes the same routes for deployable environments.
context.key_innovation: Grounded retrieval + prompt conditioning instead of fine-tuning or vector-store RAG. Parsed structured shopping signals locally (20 color variants with 'rosé'/'rose' normalization, 24 region keywords, 40+ varietals), filtered the catalog before prompting Gemini, injected only filtered results as JSON. System prompt forbids invention. Follow-up carry-forward inherits prior-turn filters on 'cheaper' / 'what about'. Progressive relaxation widens the net when no exact matches exist.
context.consultation_state_machine: useSommelierConsultation() drives 5 states: closed → greeting → listening → thinking (Vertex AI streams reply) → speaking (Cloud TTS plays, interruptible). Conversation history capped at 5 turns for prefill-token hygiene.
context.my_contribution: Solo-authored the entire monorepo: catalog parser, follow-up carry-forward, relaxation strategy, Vertex AI SSE streaming, Cloud TTS integration, proxy server with gcloud token caching, 3D boutique scene, VRM-model NPC sommelier, consultation state machine, recommendation cards, ambience audio, health checks, error classification, Playwright E2E suite. Self-directed product build.
context.scope_rationale: Recognized the interesting question was not 'can you answer wine questions' but 'does voice + retail atmosphere change the buying experience'. Extracted wine-ai-core as a workspace BEFORE adding any 3D so the shared core could be iterated in the sandbox and the 3D shell could drop onto it cleanly.

projects.name: Evolutionary Agentic Search (research, paused)
projects.description: A 5-phase research project exploring whether reranking algorithms and query-reconstruction logic can be co-evolved via LLM-driven program synthesis (RankEvolve + SkyDiscover + EvoX + SmartSearch) with fitness signals from Agentic-R's multi-turn reasoning utility. Phase 1 + Phase 2 scaffolded; paused since Mar 11 2026.
highlights: Proposed a self-improving search engine where reranking programs are evolved via LLM-driven program synthesis and query-reconstruction logic is meta-evolved, with fitness grounded in Agentic-R's per-passage multi-turn utility signals.

Designed the critical Phase 1 Fitness Bridge: compresses Agentic-R's vector-valued trajectory utility into a scalar fitness via weighted aggregation (alpha=0.3 local, 0.7 global EM), chosen over StarPO which optimizes agent policies rather than program-synthesis fitness.
Planned DeepSearchQA (900 causal-chain multi-hop tasks) over HotpotQA to stress-test dependency chains and expose reward-hacking. 7 phase docs authored; Phase 1 + 2 modules scaffolded.

context.status: Paused since Mar 11 2026. Design documentation complete (7 phase docs). Phase 1 (fitness_bridge) + Phase 2 (reranker_evolution) scaffolded in src/. Phases 3, 4, 5 not implemented.
context.problem_space: Modern search systems have human-written reranking math that hits diminishing returns as retrieval surfaces diversify. LLM-driven program synthesis can evolve ranking programs automatically, but Agentic-R's available fitness signals are multi-dimensional and multi-turn, not the scalar fitness program-synthesis loops need. The core research question: can the bridge between them be built cleanly enough that the rest of the 5-phase plan stays publishable?
context.why_paused: Competing priorities through Feb-Apr 2026: Feb FunctionGemma hackathon (2nd place), Feb PathGuard, Mar BigThink win (Auto-Eval3D), Apr Wine Voice AI + YC hackathon (HVAC Copilot finalist). Research projects need long uninterrupted blocks of focus; the hackathon season absorbed that capacity. Paused, not abandoned.
context.my_contribution: Solo: full system design, 7-phase architecture, fitness-bridge algorithm (weighted aggregation with alpha calibration), Phase 1 + 2 implementation scaffold, infrastructure setup (pyproject.toml with GPU optional-deps, pytest, ruff, CodeRabbit config).

projects.name: PathGuard Edge
projects.description: On-device spatial safety intelligence for construction workers — dual-pipeline edge AI system fusing VLM scene understanding with real-time spatial hazard detection
highlights: Architected a dual-pipeline edge AI system: a Cactus Narrator running Liquid LFM 2.5 VLM (1.6B params) on-device for scene transcription, feeding dynamic prompts into a spatial reasoning HUD.

Built a real-time hazard detection pipeline fusing Grounding DINO (zero-shot detection), SAM2 (pixel-precise segmentation), and Depth Anything V2 (distance estimation) inside an egocentric corridor ROI.
Engineered a corridor occupancy metric and state machine (Clear → Obstacle Ahead → Trip Risk) with audio alerts, outputting enriched telemetry JSON with physical risk events for site managers.

context.problem_space: 800+ construction workers die annually from falls/trips. Cloud-based solutions fail because job sites lack reliable connectivity. Spatial safety intelligence must live on the edge.
context.architecture_decision: Dual pipeline: VLM generates scene-specific prompts (avoiding static/hallucinated detection lists), then spatial pipeline performs corridor-bounded hazard reasoning. Classical CV fallback runs every frame; DINO runs on a schedule.
context.key_innovation: Corridor ROI — a trapezoid representing the worker's egocentric walking lane. All hazard reasoning is bounded to this region, eliminating false positives from objects outside the path.
context.integration_detail: Enriched telemetry JSON bridges Cactus semantic report with PathGuard physical data: peak corridor occupancy, depth buckets (near/mid/far), and trip risk event timestamps.
context.hackathon_context: UMD × Ironsite Startup Shell Hackathon (Feb 2026). $17,500 prize pool ($10k/$5k/$2.5k). ~60 participants. Focused on spatial/physical intelligence and world models. Submissions required GitHub repo, detailed README, and 3-5 min demo video. Applied Cactus SDK knowledge gained from FunctionGemma hackathon the same weekend.
context.my_contribution: Built the Cactus Narrator integration (on-device VLM via Liquid LFM 2.5 on Apple Neural Engine), wrote the hybrid routing logic (confidence-based on-device/cloud escalation with cooldown timer), created the dynamic prompt generation pipeline (VLM scene descriptions → Gemini extraction → GroundedDINO-compatible prompt list), and merged both sub-projects into one unified codebase under extreme time pressure. Also assisted Suraj Rao and Keshav Naram on the PathGuard HUD side (corridor reasoning, state machine). Recorded and narrated the demo video.

Baseline started at ~50% F1, iterated through 62.3% → 65.3% → final 0.99 F1 by fixing confidence_threshold, cloud_handoff handling, and argument post-processing.

projects.name: AI Resume Chatbot
projects.description: Production AI agent answering recruiter questions — 10 backend services, 5 LLM-as-a-Judge evaluators, zero SDKs. Live at chat.rayhanpatel.com
highlights: Built a service-oriented AI agent with 10 backend services (Intent Classifier, Agent, Memory, Tracer, Rate Limiter, Session, Lead Capture, Job Extractor, Job Parser, Prompt Generator) and graceful degradation — chat continues even if every external service is down.

Replaced the blocking Google GenAI SDK with direct httpx HTTP/2 calls to the Gemini REST API, implementing async connection pooling (20 keepalive, 100 max connections), a thread-safe TTLCache with deadlock prevention, and pure ASGI middleware to avoid Starlette's BaseHTTPMiddleware hanging bug.

Deployed 5 automated LLM-as-a-Judge evaluators (Hallucination, Relevance, Conciseness, Helpfulness, Toxicity) via Langfuse at 100% sampling with zero latency impact — evaluation model (Gemini 2.5 Flash) is separate from generation model to avoid self-bias.

context.architecture: Split Architecture: Frontend on Vercel (through Cloudflare DNS+SSL), Backend on Railway (direct API access bypassing Cloudflare to avoid SSE timeout limits). Service-Oriented Architecture — thin FastAPI route handlers delegate to rich domain services. Every external dependency (Mem0, Supabase, Langfuse) wrapped in a service class with 'enabled' flag that fails gracefully.
context.httpx_decision: The official google-genai Python SDK uses synchronous transport internally, causing blocking I/O and threading issues with asyncio. Replaced with direct httpx HTTP/2 calls to Gemini REST API (httpx >=0.28). Provides full async support, connection pooling (20 keepalive, 100 max), and explicit control over timeouts and retries.
context.ttlcache_decision: TTLCache extends OrderedDict with threading.Lock on all public methods. Internal operations use super().__delitem__() and super().__setitem__() to bypass overridden methods that would re-acquire the lock, preventing deadlocks.
context.security_layers: 8-layer SSRF-protected job URL fetcher, Cloudflare Turnstile bot detection (Managed Mode), HTML stripping via @field_validator(mode='before') on all Pydantic models, secrets.compare_digest() for constant-time admin auth, prompt injection defense with <<<JOB_DESCRIPTION_START>>> markers.
context.intent_classification: Off-topic queries classified and declined BEFORE the expensive agent call. Uses Gemini Flash (cheapest model) with temperature=0.1 for deterministic output. Defaults to job_related on any failure.
context.eval_pipeline: 5 LLM-as-a-Judge evaluators run server-side in Langfuse at 100% sampling: Hallucination, Relevance, Conciseness, Helpfulness, Toxicity. Evaluation model (Gemini 2.5 Flash) differs from generation model (Gemini 2.0 Flash) to avoid self-bias. Zero latency impact on users.
context.key_features_summary: 25+ features: real-time SSE streaming, dual LLM fallback (Vertex AI → AI Studio), job URL extraction + LLM-powered parsing, dynamic starter prompts, semantic memory (Mem0), session persistence (Supabase + TTLCache fallback), dark/light theme, share conversation, keyboard shortcuts, lead capture (Google Sheets), WCAG accessibility, React ErrorBoundary, OG+Twitter Card SEO, iOS mobile polish.
context.tech_stack_detail: Backend: FastAPI >=0.115, uvicorn >=0.34, httpx >=0.28, Pydantic >=2.10, mem0ai >=1.0.2, langfuse >=3.12, supabase >=2.27, tenacity >=8.2, google-auth >=2.27. Frontend: React 18.3, Vite 5.4, TailwindCSS 3.4, lucide-react, react-markdown 10.1, remark-gfm 4.0.

projects.name: AlphaFoundry (Quant Engine)
projects.description: Factor-based quantitative investment strategy engine using XGBoost and Fama-French factors
highlights: Architected a rolling-window backtesting engine that combines Fama-French 5-factor analysis with XGBoost Learning-to-Rank, achieving a Sharpe Ratio of 0.95 (vs SPY 0.85).
Built a production-grade FastAPI inference service for real-time asset ranking.
Implemented Walk-Forward validation to prevent look-ahead bias in financial time-series modeling.

context.problem_space: Retail investors lack access to systematic, factor-based strategies that hedge funds use. Most open-source quant tools focus on single-factor or momentum only.
